home.heroSubtitle: Open, view, convert and manage almost any file — on your own hardware. Tools that can run in your browser do, so your files never even leave your device.
home.toolsSubtitle: Jump straight in — tools that can run on your device do, so your files stay with you.
home.toolsEmptyBody: The first tools land here as modules ship. Search is ready whenever they do.
home.categoriesTitle: Built around what you work on
home.categoriesSubtitle: Every category is a module. Drop a file anywhere and Omnio shows what it can do.
home.whyPrivacyBody: Browser-tier tools process files entirely on your device. Nothing is uploaded, tracked or retained — and analytics are off unless you turn them on.
home.whySelfHostedBody: One Docker Compose file brings up the whole platform on your own machine, NAS or server. It works fully air-gapped.
home.whyViewerBody: Images, video, PDF, code, archives, documents — drop any file and see it instantly, with every available action one click away.
home.whyOpenBody: AGPL-licensed, with a module SDK designed so a contributor can ship a polished tool in an afternoon.
home.whyFastBody: Instant search, a command palette, keyboard shortcuts everywhere, and interfaces that respond in milliseconds.
home.roadmapSubtitle: Omnio is built milestone by milestone, in the open, with the repository releasable at every commit.
home.faqA1: Yes — structurally, not just by promise. Tools that can run in your browser never upload your files at all, and the badge on each tool tells you where it runs. Everything else stays on hardware you control, with uploads expiring automatically.
home.faqQ2: What do I need to run it?
home.faqA2: Docker and Docker Compose. One command brings up the web app, API, worker, database and queue. A small home server or NAS is plenty.
home.faqA3: Omnio is open source under AGPL-3.0. Self-host it, modify it, use it for anything — the license only asks that improvements to the platform stay open.
home.faqQ4: Can I add my own tools?
home.faqA4: That's the whole design. Every tool is a module with a manifest; the SDK, docs and scaffolder are built so your first tool takes an afternoon, not a weekend.
